title: Rocky Calmus Wins the 2001 Butkus Award for Oklahoma
question: When did Rocky Calmus win the Butkus Award?
answer: Rocky Calmus won the Butkus Award on Dec. 7, 2001, as the nation's best linebacker. It was Oklahoma's third Butkus Award and the first since Brian Bosworth won it in 1985 and 1986.
summary: Rocky Calmus won the 2001 Butkus Award, OU's first since Brian Bosworth, after a 117-tackle senior year. Dick Butkus himself handed him the trophy in Orlando.
body: Fifteen years after Brian Bosworth's second Butkus Award, another Sooner linebacker got his hands on the trophy. On Dec. 7, 2001, in Orlando, Rocky Calmus was named the best linebacker in college football, and Dick Butkus himself presented the award.

Calmus, a Jenks native, finished his senior year with a team-high 117 tackles, 15 tackles for loss, four sacks, two fumble recoveries and an interception. He was the centerpiece of a defense that ranked fourth nationally in both scoring and total defense. The winner was chosen by an independent 28-member selection committee of media members, and Calmus beat out fellow finalists E.J. Henderson of Maryland and Robert Thomas of UCLA.

OU's coaching staff made the trip, too. Bob Stoops, associate head coach Mike Stoops and co-defensive coordinator Brent Venables were all on hand in Orlando, along with Calmus' family, to watch one of their cornerstone players accept the honor.

The award capped a remarkable run. Calmus was a consensus All-American in both 2000 and 2001 and a key starter on the 2000 defense that held Florida State to two points in a 13-2 Orange Bowl win for the national championship. He also took home the Jack Lambert Trophy in 2001.

The Tennessee Titans picked Calmus in the third round of the 2002 NFL Draft, and he played for Tennessee from 2002 to 2004. His 2001 trophy was Oklahoma's third Butkus Award, and Teddy Lehman would make it four just two years later.
